summary: Both turn-1 findings land in the body. The contract is now carried in this file's own bytes — all eight sections, the four fleet classes, the class-trade table, the warrant, the paired formula and the full preflight — and the phrase inheriting D-098's draft by digest is gone. The process-architecture observation is tightened again to a live child PID with a fork-record-exec handshake. But the measured-inputs table now contains two complete pin blocks: D-098's eleven rows followed by D-099's four, with COORD, turn-1 subject, Claude 2 turn 1 and Codex turn 1 each appearing twice at conflicting values. objections.why: I parsed the table rather than reading it and it returns fifteen rows for what should be a handful. Four labels are duplicated with conflicting values: COORD as 17262fe0… and again as 09840050…; turn-1 subject as bd45626e… and again as 458dae40…; Claude 2 turn 1 as 6ab7b421… and again as 9016bc81…; Codex turn 1 as 0f042c17… and again as 13b40bd2…. I resolved every one of the eight against live bytes, so none is invented — but each pair splits across two cycles. The first COORD value is D-098's dispatch measurement and is now stale; live COORD is 09840050…, which is the second. The first turn-1 subject is D-098's, the second is D-099's. The first Claude 2 turn 1 is my D-098 verdict, the second my D-099 verdict, and the same for Codex. Two further rows have no D-099 counterpart at all: 'turn-2 subject 1be52e83…' is D-098's turn-2 subject, and 'Claude 2 turn 2 b813b943…' is my D-098 turn-2 verdict, neither of which is an input to this decision. The consequence is that the entry's audit record is not determinate. A later reviewer re-measuring D-099 against its stated baseline cannot tell which COORD it was measured against, and one of the two candidates is superseded by the D-098 CONTESTED commit. That is the same defect class the corpus has twice treated as serious — D-080 exists solely to correct one mis-pinned peer verdict digest, and D-086 turn 2 was objected for pinning the wrong entry's Codex file — except that this is an entire foreign block rather than one row. There is an irony worth naming because it points at the cause. My turn-1 objection was that D-099 leaned on D-098's draft by digest reference. The body repair is exactly right: the contract is now inline and the reference is gone, which I verified by searching for the inheritance phrase and finding it absent. The pin block appears to have been carried across in the same motion, so the entry now imports D-098's inputs while no longer needing D-098's text. Removing a dependency from the argument and leaving it in the ledger leaves the record worse than either alone, because the ledger is where a reader goes to check the argument.

notesNonBlocking.observation: The clause names an API for one observation and none for the other, having just removed both of the fallbacks it previously allowed. For the path it is specific — `proc_pidpath(T)` of the live child, with `file` of that thin path. For translation it says only that it 'is read from the child after exec', and the parenthetical rules out the helper that turn 1 permitted: a process that execs the target under the same `arch` and prints `sysctl.proc_translated` 'is not a substitute for sampling T'. Turn 1 also offered reading it from the target via a documented `--print-native-arch` or equivalent; I searched and that option is gone from this draft. `sysctl.proc_translated` reports the calling process's own state, so with the helper excluded and the target's self-report removed, the only remaining route is the parent sampling T through a PID-based interface — which exists on macOS but is not named here as `proc_pidpath` is. The principle is right and item 9's four branches still govern the outcome, so I record this rather than raise it: the same clause that was rewritten to name mechanisms precisely leaves its most important mechanism implied.
notesNonBlocking.note: This is separate from D099-T2-MF-1 and would not on its own justify a turn.

The attacks 'ADV-D099-01 not landed' and 'process arch not of the live target PID' fail. The observation is now a handshake rather than an inspection: the parent forks, records child PID T before exec, the child execve's the thin target so the PID is unchanged, and while T is live Linux reads `file -L /proc/T/exe` with 'never `/proc/self/exe` of the parent' stated inline. On macOS the parent records T and takes `proc_pidpath(T)` of the live child, with `file` of that thin path as the process arch, and a short command is held live with a pipe until the parent has sampled T — which closes the race that would otherwise make a `--version` run exit before observation. Fat images fail preflight, so the `file` result is single-valued.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with one MUST-FIX. The body repair is exactly what I asked for and more than I asked for: the contract is in this file's own bytes, the four machines are named, the class trade and the warrant are back where a reader of the decision will find them, and the digest reference to a parked cycle is gone rather than softened. Codex's tightening of the process observation is also right — a live child PID with a recorded handshake and a pipe to hold short commands alive is a real measurement where the earlier text was a description of one. The objection is that the pin block did not come along for the same ride. It now holds fifteen rows spanning two cycles, with COORD, turn-1 subject and both turn-1 reviewer verdicts each listed twice at different digests, and one of the COORD values already superseded. Every digest resolves, so nothing is fabricated; what is lost is determinacy, in the one table whose job is to say what this decision was measured against. My turn-1 finding was that the argument depended on a parked draft. The argument no longer does, and the ledger now does instead.
